adds.title: Nigeria: Sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics — Country Policy and Information Note (UK Home Office, June 2025)
adds.summary: The UK Home Office's June 2025 country note carries Kaduna's own row in its twelve-state Sharia penalties table (section 8.4.3, ILGA-derived): Kaduna's Sharia Penal Code Law (2002) with death by stoning as the maximum for liwat (sodomy) and same-sex acts between women punishable 'at the discretion of the qadi (Sharia court judge)'. Section 3.1.6 and 8.2.19 add that Kaduna separately adopted its own secular Penal Code in 2017, whose Section 259 punishes 'unnatural offences' - sodomy, lesbianism, bestiality - with up to 21 years' imprisonment and a fine, above the federal 14-year ceiling. Dated government confirmation of the two-layer criminalisation this record claims: a harsher Kaduna-specific secular statute plus a parallel Sharia layer applying to Muslims.

adds.title: Sharia Implementation in Northern Nigeria 1999-2006: A Sourcebook, Vol. IV, Ch. 4 Part III — The Sharia Penal Codes (Ostien, ed.)
adds.summary: Ostien's annotated volume lists Kaduna's Sharia Penal Code Law 2002, Law No. 4 of 2002, signed into law and coming into operation on 21 June 2002 (Kaduna State Gazette No. 17 Vol. 36, 4 July 2002, pp. A15-A108, bound with the Sharia Criminal Procedure Code), and its annotation records that Kaduna is one of only three states whose enacted text states 'Whoever commits the offence of sodomy shall be punished with stoning to death (rajm)' - with no unmarried/married graduation - while the lesbianism offence is left to ta'azir (discretionary punishment). Enactment-level evidence that Kaduna's Sharia layer is its own promulgated parallel criminal code carrying the bloc's capital ceiling for men's same-sex acts, confirming this record's stacked-architecture finding without relying on umbrella coverage.

adds.title: Sharia Implementation in Northern Nigeria 1999-2006: A Sourcebook, Vol. IV, Ch. 4 Part III — The Sharia Penal Codes (Ostien, ed.)
adds.summary: Ostien's annotated volume lists Katsina's Sharia Penal Code Law 2001, Law No. 2 of 2001, coming into operation on 20 June 2001 and gazetted in Katsina State Gazette Vol. 12 No. 23, 27 August 2001, and its annotation records Katsina among the three states (with Kaduna and Kebbi) whose sodomy text reads 'Whoever commits the offence of sodomy shall be punished with stoning to death (rajm)', while the lesbianism offence is punished by stoning to death - footnote 183 shows only Kano and Katsina reaching that capital maximum, against the harmonised code's base of 50 lashes and up to six months. Independent academic source for this record's claim that Katsina is one of only two states whose law carries death as the maximum for same-sex acts between women as well as men.

adds.title: Nigeria: Sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics — Country Policy and Information Note (UK Home Office, June 2025)
adds.summary: The UK Home Office's June 2025 country note carries Kebbi's own row in its twelve-state Sharia penalties table (section 8.4.3): Kebbi's Penal Code (Amendment) Law (Law No. 21) (2000) with death by stoning for liwat (sodomy) and up to 50 lashes with imprisonment for up to 6 months for same-sex acts between women - the standard bloc penalty for women's conduct rather than the Kano/Katsina capital maximum. Dated government confirmation that Kebbi's Sharia layer extends criminalisation to acts between women, matching this record's claim that the state's code is broader in scope and harsher than the federal statute for Muslim defendants.

adds.title: Sharia Implementation in Northern Nigeria 1999-2006: A Sourcebook, Vol. IV, Ch. 4 Part III — The Sharia Penal Codes (Ostien, ed.)
adds.summary: Ostien's annotated volume lists Kebbi's Penal Code (Amendment) Law 2000, Law No. 21 of 2000, signed into law and coming into operation on 1 December 2000 (Kebbi State Gazette Vol. 2 No. 1, Supplement, 31 December 2000), and its annotations record Kebbi as one of three states (with Kaduna and Katsina) whose enacted text states 'Whoever commits the offence of sodomy shall be punished with stoning to death (rajm)', while lesbianism follows the harmonised code's 50 lashes and up to six months' imprisonment. Enactment-level confirmation that Kebbi adopted its own Sharia penal layer in the 1999-2002 wave with a capital ceiling for men's acts and women's same-sex conduct criminalised, grounding this record's jurisdictional-difference finding in Kebbi's own statute.
